findings.title: Prophetic gifts placed under divine knowledge
findings.claim: 17:55 presents prophetic differentiation as an allotment placed by the Lord who knows where His message belongs, not as prestige autonomously claimed by people; David's named Zabur makes one differentiated prophetic gift concrete as a written instrument.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins divine knowledge, partitive comparison, prophets, and David's received book. In 6:124, a demand for the same messenger-gift meets the statement that God knows best where to place His message; 2:253 describes distinct modes of address and degrees, while 2:251 and 27:15 identify David's bestowed gifts and knowledge. The revelation sequence in 4:163 and the written registers in 54:52 connect the named Zabur to prophetic communication and preserved text. These contacts turn some over others from a bare scalar ranking into divine assignment of differing communicative gifts.
findings.reader_payoff: The comparison becomes a distribution of prophetic roles and gifts under one source, with David's book as a concrete textual instrument rather than evidence of self-originating status.
findings.containment: The focus gives no complete rank order or assignment of each prophet's function. Connected ayat provide parallels, not target morphology; the root-family resonance of prophet with news is not a claim that the focus word simply means report. The written-register contact supports preservation only as an analogy, not a physical lining or a reconstruction of the Zabur's full contents.

epistemic.reason: The citable cross-run candidate is trusted and its core is directly aligned to focus words; the broader connection-based lexical and role resonances are qualified because target morphology is not supplied for connected ayat.

findings.title: A bestowed distinction can test its receivers
findings.claim: The focus's preference and bestowal can be read within a wider pattern in which divine gifts honor recipients while also testing them and exposing audience response; this does not make David's Zabur itself a test-sign.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies the acts of preferring and giving. In 6:165, degrees are joined to being tested in what God has given; 2:87 and 2:253 show recipients and audiences responding differently to bestowed books or signs. Their contact turns the focus's gift from a static badge of honor into an entrusted distinction whose reception can matter.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold honor and accountability together: a gift may mark a recipient while still revealing how it is received and used.
findings.containment: The connected passages concern degrees and gifts generally or signs given to other messengers. They do not say that the Zabur was specifically a sign or trial, and no testing function from Jesus's clear signs is transferred to David's book.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows supply exact target Arabic for the testing and response pattern, but no target morphology; the reading is a bounded contextual resonance rather than an attributed HFT activation.

branch_activations.carrier: Atayna states that David was given the Zabur.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 6:165 explicitly joins testing with what God has given; 2:87 and 2:253 show books or signs granted to messengers followed by differing audience responses.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's recipient-directed giving meets contexts where gifts become occasions of testing and response.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The act of giving can carry both honor and accountability, rather than functioning only as a prestige marker.
branch_activations.boundary: The cited tests and responses are not stated of David or the Zabur specifically.

This makes David's book more than a biographical gift in the global reading: its stated content touches the earth already named in the focus.
findings.reader_payoff: The book gift becomes a point where divine knowledge of the earth and a future claim about the earth meet.
findings.containment: Only the particular promise stated in 21:105 is connected here. The focus and connection do not disclose the Zabur's full contents, textual voice, history, or every detail of the inheritance claim.

epistemic.reason: The supplied connection gives the exact Arabic contact between Zabur and earth, but target morphology and a wider account of the book are not supplied.

findings.title: Divine differentiation and undivided belief
findings.claim: 17:55 reports divine preference among prophets, while 2:136, 2:285, 3:84, and 4:152 describe believers affirming all messengers without selectively believing in some and rejecting others; the two statements concern distinct acts and can stand together.
findings.mechanism: The focus's some-over-some comparison meets confession passages that say believers make no distinction among messengers in their faith. Their contact keeps divine differentiation distinct from human selective acceptance, so a reported gift or rank is not a license to reject another prophet.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the comparison without turning it into a rule of selective belief: divine bestowal and the believer's affirmation of all messengers remain separate claims.
findings.containment: The confession passages address belief and acceptance; they do not deny the focus's report that God preferred some prophets. This is a contextual counter-reading held alongside the focus, not a harmonization that erases either statement.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows provide exact target Arabic for the confessional formula, but no target morphology; the reading is limited to the stated distinction between divine preference and human belief.

branch_activations.carrier: Faddalna and the paired partitive terms state a divine comparison among prophets.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The four connected passages state that believers affirm the messengers without distinguishing among them in faith.
branch_activations.activation: The same prophetic field is viewed from two distinct agents: God differentiates in bestowal, while believers are commanded not to discriminate in affirmation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Divine differentiation does not entail selective acceptance of prophets by believers.
branch_activations.boundary: These contexts concern confessional response; they do not reverse or cancel the focus's statement about God's preference.

findings.title: Prophetic office as a guidance path
findings.claim: The prophet carrier in 17:55 can be colored by a route-to-destination analogy when 42:52 describes revealed guidance as a straight path; this makes prophetic communication perceptible as guidance, not merely distinction.
findings.mechanism: The focus names prophets, and 42:52 independently describes a straight path and guidance in the setting of revelation. Their contact allows the route branch to resonate with prophetic communication as guidance toward a destination.
findings.reader_payoff: The prophetic comparison can be heard not only as differentiated honor but as differentiated service within a guidance-bearing message.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory analogy. 42:52 addresses Muhammad directly; it does not say that the word prophets literally means road or assign the exact same guidance task to every prophet.

epistemic.reason: The connection supplies a clear path image but target morphology is absent and the transfer from one direct address to the plural focus is analogical.

findings.title: An exploratory nurturing resonance

findings.mechanism: The focus's Rabb carrier has a supplied nurture-and-growth branch. The independent description of some messengers being raised in degrees supplies a development image that can meet that branch, making the divine allotment imaginable as fostering distinct capacities.
findings.reader_payoff: The comparison may be perceived as more than placing one messenger above another: it can suggest capacities fostered under the care of the Lord who knows and places the message.
findings.containment: This is analogical, not a literal growth claim. 2:253 reports degrees but does not describe a staged upbringing or training process; Rabb remains Lord, and no specific developmental sequence is inferred.

epistemic.reason: The degree language is an independent contact, but interpreting it through the nurture branch is a bounded analogy and target morphology for the connection is not supplied.
